title: Proteomics protocol for obtaining extracellular vesicle from human plasma using asymmetrical flow field-flow fractionation technology
protocol: Take plasma from -80°C and thaw it at 4°C.
Dilute 200 μL of plasma with PBS at a 1:1 v/v ratio.
Centrifuge the sample at 300 × g for 10 min at 4°C to remove intact cells.
Carefully transfer the supernatant into a new 1.5 mL tube.
Centrifuge the supernatant at 4200 × g for 20 min at 4°C to remove large cell debris, apoptosis body, and platelet.
Carefully transfer the supernatant into a new 1.5 mL tube for the following enrichment of EVs.
Store the supernatant at -80°C if not used immediately.
Open the monitoring software ASTRA (version 5.3.4).
Right-click on “Experiments” and create a new template.
Set duration time and check “LS 11”, “UV”, “dRI”.
Click the blue triangle to start sample injection.
Suck up 300 μL of prepared sample solution using a needle.
Insert the needle into the injector.
Rotate the injector to "Load".
Inject the sample solution.
Rotate the injector to "Inject".
Collect peak 4 effluent according to UV 280, LS 11, dRI signals.
Observe the budding of EVs peak and collect EVs effluent after 5 seconds.
Wash the system for about 20 minutes before loading the next sample.
Concentrate collected effluent to about 150 μL using a 3 kDa MWCO membrane filter at 3000 × g for 3 hours at 4°C.
Alternatively, concentrate with a 10 kDa MWCO membrane filter for about 30 minutes.
Store concentrated effluent at -80°C for several months.
Quantify the protein concentration using a Pierce BCA Protein Assay Kit following the manufacturer’s instructions.
Dilute the EVs sample twice with 10% SDS solution.
Heat the diluted EVs sample at 95°C for 10 minutes.
Mix 50 parts of Reagent A with 1 part of Reagent B to prepare the BCA working reagent.
Calculate the volume required for Reagent A using the formula: (number of samples × 3 + number of Protein Standards × 8 × 3 + extra samples) × 200 μL Reagent A.
Calculate the volume required for Reagent B using the formula: (number of samples × 3 + number of Protein Standards × 8 × 3 + extra samples) × 4 μL Reagent B.
Add 200 μL of the working reagent to each well of the 96-well plate.
Pipette 4 μL of water into the 96-well plate.
Pipette 7 different concentrations of bovine serum albumin (BSA) standard solution into the 96-well plate successively.
Pipette EVs samples with triplicates into the 96-well plate successively.
Gently pipet each sample up and down several times to mix well.
Incubate the plate at 37°C for 30 min.
Measure the absorbance values of samples at 562 nm after incubation.
Pierce any air bubbles in sample wells with a tip of 10 μL pipette.
Separate 15 μg of proteins on SDS-PAGE gel at a constant voltage of 200 V.
Immerse the PVDF membrane in 100% methanol for 30 s to activate it.
Transfer the protein to the PVDF membrane at a constant current of 200 mA.
Wash the PVDF membrane using 1 × TBST for 5 min.
Block the membrane with 5% milk for at least 2 h.
Incubate the membrane with primary antibody (diluted with 5% milk in the ratio of 1:1000).
Wash the membrane using 1 × TBST for 10 min three times.
Incubate the membrane with secondary antibody (diluted with 5% milk in the ratio of 1:10000).
Wash the membrane using 1 × TBST for 10 min three times.
Mix the developer solution A and B in a ratio of 1:1, then drip the mixed solution to the membrane and develop the membrane.
Prepare the EV sample for TEM analysis.
Put the carbon-coated copper grids into the glow instrument.
Vacuumize the instrument for 4 min.
Charge the carbon-coated copper grids with glow for 30 s.
Place 5 μL of the EV sample onto the coated side of the grid.
Allow the sample to adsorb for 1 min.
Absorb away the drop using filter paper.
Wash the copper grid with negative staining solution (2% uranyl acetate).
Absorb away the wash solution using filter paper.
Add 5 μL of negative staining solution to the sample side of the grid.
Incubate for 1 min to stain the background around the EVs.
Air dry the grid.
Solubilize a total of 50 μg protein in 8 M urea/50 mM NH4HCO3.
Reduce the solubilized protein with 20 mM DTT for 1 h at 37°C.
Add 40 mM IAM to the sample and incubate in the dark for 45 min at 20°C–25°C.
Add Lys C at an enzyme/protein ratio of 1:50 (w/w) for 3 h at 37°C.
Dilute the sample with 25 mM NH4HCO3 to a final concentration of <1.5 M urea.
Add trypsin at an enzyme/protein ratio of 1:50 (w/w).
Incubate the sample in a ThermoMixer F1.5 for heating and mixing at 37°C for 12–18 h.
Use a final concentration of 0.1% formic acid to stop the protein digestion.
Desalt the sample with an Oasis HLB 1 cc Vac cartridge using a vacuum manifold.
Wash the cartridge with 1 mL methanol and 1 mL 75% acetonitrile/0.1% FA.
Equilibrate the cartridge twice with 1 mL 0.1% FA.
Load the sample solution for 3–4 times.
Wash the cartridge twice with 1 mL 0.1% FA.
Elute the sample successively with 400 μL of 20% ACN/0.1% FA, 40% ACN/0.1% FA, and 60% ACN/0.1% FA.
Dry the eluted sample in a centrifugal vacuum concentrator.
Redissolve the desalted peptides in 50 μL of 100 mM HEPES (pH 8.5).
Equilibrate TMT6-plex label reagents to 20°C–25°C for about 30 minutes.
Label peptides with a TMT6-plex kit according to the manufacturer’s protocol.
Store TMT-labeled peptides at -20°C for several days or at -80°C for several weeks.
Calculate labeling efficiency.
Mix 2 μL of each labeled sample.
Dry the mixed samples.
Redissolve dried samples in 10 μL of 0.1% FA.
Desalt the redissolved samples using a μC18 ZipTip.
Dry desalted samples again.
Redissolve dried samples with 15 μL of 0.1% FA.
Centrifuge the sample at 20,000 × g for about 30 min.
Transfer the supernatant into a new autosampler vial.
Load the supernatant onto an EASY-nLC 1000 HPLC system coupled to Nanospray Flex Ion Source and Q Exactive Mass Spectrometer.
Elute peptides through a C18 trap column using mobile phase A (0.1% FA) and B (ACN/0.1% FA).
Separate peptides on an in-house packed C18 capillary column at a flow rate of 310 nL/min with the following gradient: 4%-10% solvent B for 5 min.
Continue the separation using a linear increase to higher percentages of solvent B over the remaining time.
Prepare a solution using solvent B according to the gradient:
Increase from 10%-22% over 50 minutes.
Increase from 22%-32% over 15 minutes.
Increase from 32%-90% over 1 minute.
Maintain at 90% for 7 minutes.
Operate Q Exactive in data-dependent MS/MS mode using the settings:
Scan 20 most intense precursors from 300 to 1600 m/z at a resolution of 70,000.
Isolate precursor ions with an isolation width of 2 m/z and set dynamic exclusion time to 50 seconds for fragmentation with normalized collision energy of 27%.
Acquire MS/MS spectra at a resolution of 17,500 at m/z 200 with a target value of 5e4 and a maximum injection time of 80 ms.
Process the raw data in Proteome Discoverer 2.2 using a regular workflow.
Search the raw data against the Uniprot human protein database including a common contaminant list.
Use the Sequest HT search engine for protein identification with trypsin as enzyme, allowing two missed cleavages.
Set mass tolerance of precursor and product ions to 10 ppm and 0.02 Da respectively.

Specify carbamidomethylation on cysteine as fixed modification; specify TMT-labeling (lysine and peptide N-terminus), methionine oxidation, and acetylation of the N-terminus as variable modifications.
Set false discovery rate (FDR) to 1% for both protein and peptide identifications.
Remove contaminant proteins before downstream analysis.
Designate TMT labeling of lysine and peptide N-terminus as dynamic modifications.
Calculate the labeling efficiency of TMT on peptides using the formula: Labeling efficiency = (number of TMT-labeled peptides) / (number of total peptides) × 100%.
Ensure the labeling efficiency is higher than 95%.
Calculate the total signal intensity at peptide or peptide spectral matches levels.
Adjust the mixing ratio of each sample to make the total signal intensity of each sample equally.
Combine the labeled samples according to the adjusted mixing ratio of each sample.
Dry the mixture in a centrifugal vacuum concentrator.
Redissolve the dried mixture with 200 μL of 0.1% FA.
Desalt the mixture using an Oasis HLB 1 cc Vac cartridge.
Dry the elution in a centrifugal vacuum concentrator.
Store the dried elution at −20°C for several days if needed.
Redissolve the dried elution with 100 μL of buffer A (2% ACN/0.1% NH4OH).
Centrifuge the sample at 20,000 × g for 20 minutes.
Transfer the supernatant into a new tube.
Inject the sample onto a C18 column.
Elute the sample using buffers A and B with a constant flow rate of 0.7 mL/min.
Collect fractions at 90-second intervals during elution.
Dry all collected fractions in a centrifugal vacuum concentrator.
Redissolve each dried fraction with 50 μL of 0.1% FA.
Centrifuge the redissolved samples at 20,000 × g for 30 minutes.
Transfer the supernatants into new autosampler vials.
Analyze the fractionated peptide samples using LC-MS/MS.
Tryptic peptides digested from 50 μg protein are redissolved with 100 μL 0.1% FA.
Transfer 50 μL of the peptide solution into a new tube and add 50 μL 0.1% FA to dilute the concentration.
Prepare a dilution series of the peptide standard to generate a standard curve.
Mix 50 parts of Reagent A with 48 part of Reagent B and 2 part of Reagent C (A:B:C = 50:48:2, volume ratio).
Add 180 μL working reagent to each well of the 96-well plate.
Pipette 20 μL of water into the 96-well plate.
Pipette 7 different concentrations of peptide standard and peptide samples with triplicates into the 96-well plate successively.
Incubate the plate at 22°C for 30 min or 37°C for 15 min.
Measure the absorbance value at 480 nm using a Varioskan Flash spectral scanning multimode reader.
Calculate the peptide concentration of each sample according to the standard curve.
Take 1 μg peptide of each sample and mix together.
Spit in 10 × iRT peptide into the mixed peptide sample.
Use 1 μg of mixture for data-dependent MS/MS analysis.
Acquire full MS scans at a resolution of 60,000 at m/z 200 across the mass range of 350–1500 m/z with an AGC of 4e5 and maximum injection time of 50 ms.
Acquire MS/MS spectra at a resolution of 15,000 at m/z 200, an isolation window of 1.6, a collision energy of 30%, and an AGC target value of 5e4 with a maximum injection time of 22 ms.
Generate library from Pulsar search engine in SpectroDive™ 10.4.
Click “Generate Library from Pulsar / Search Archives….”
Add runs from file by clicking “Add Runs from File…” and upload the obtained DDA raw data.
Select a FASTA file by clicking “Fasta File…” such as human Swiss-Prot FASTA database.
Set enzyme as trypsin/P in search settings.
Set carbamidomethyl (C) to a fixed modification.
Set acetyl (Protein N-term) and oxidation (M) to variable modifications.
Include b, y ion types.
Take an unscheduled PRM for RT calibration if necessary.
Analyze raw data from unscheduled PRM as a new RT calibration run and select it.
Build the PRM data acquisition method in Xcalibur.
Select “PRM iRT-Kit” below “LC Calibration”.
Choose the modified panel below “Panels”.
Choose the generated calibration run below “Choose RT Calibration Run”.
Modify specific parameters in “3) Export Method”.
Export the new method by clicking “Export Method”.
Import the target list in Xcalibur for each sample.
Monitor 1 μg of each sample according to the exported precursor list using PRM.
Acquire full MS scans at a resolution of 60,000 at m/z 200 with an AGC of 4e5 and maximum injection time of 20 ms.
Acquire MS/MS spectra at a resolution of 30,000 at m/z 200, isolation window of 1, collision energy of 30%, AGC target value of 2e5 with a maximum injection time of 80 ms.
Collect PRM data using the established method.
Analyze PRM data for precursors deviating from retention time and adjust if necessary.
Click “Analysis” and “Set up Targeted Analysis from File…” in SpectroDive.
Upload PRM raw data and assign the established panel.
Select search and extraction settings schema for PRM analysis.
Specify condition, replicates, and other information of the raw data following the wizard instructions.
Manually confirm confidence and quantitative area of the spectrum.
Right-click on file name and select "Group by protein" to facilitate verification based on protein name.
Filter data by entering protein/gene name in Node Text Filter for convenient analysis of specific proteins.
Display MS2 XIC and MS2 XIC Alignment in upper and lower panels for multiple data screening.
Manually screen precursors and their fragments in the MS2 XIC panel.
Right-click on the fragment and select “Exclude” or “Remove” in the node or all runs for precursors and fragments to exclude.
Manually adjust the green dotted lines representing the start and end points of the peak area calculations for quantitative area range adjustment.
Recalculate Q values by clicking “Recalculate Qvalues” for qualitative analysis after right-clicking on the name of the experiment.
Refresh post analysis by clicking “Refresh Post Analysis”.
Export the "Run Pivot Report" from the “Report” module.
Export the “Normal Report” from the “Report” module.
